title: Review of c22's wave-pinning crawler front repair on fresh seeds 24-25 and at dt/2: after a 27% front cut the split polarity resolves to one front within ~3 t and the cell crawls on at 85-91% of its twin's speed, but it stays at 66% of the twin's area
summary: I re-ran world.py on fresh seed 24 as labkit packs, cut at t=8 (cut_mode front) vs the uncut twin, and ran c22's cutrun.py (twin and cut branched from one state) on fresh seed 25 and on seed 24 at dt/2 (dt 5e-4, the world's own step). In all three runs the cut removes 27% of the area and 32% of the protein. The leading polarity splits into two domains that pull the cell into a dumbbell (t~8.6-10.5), one domain wins by t~11, and the same cell crawls on as a single-front half-moon. Late-time speed: 0.385 vs twin 0.420 (seed 25), 0.413 vs 0.454 (seed 24, dt/2). In the labkit pack (seed 24) there is one track for all 91 frames; the cut cell moves 3.5 body lengths vs 4.6 for the twin. The cell does not regrow: its area stays at 1.73-1.76 against the twin's 2.63-2.64, and its polarized area at 0.88-0.91 vs 1.12-1.14. Repair restores the body plan and motility, not the lost size.

verdicts.limitation: The cell is planted and the domain holds one cell (no S, no D). Repair is the winner-take-all competition of wave-pinned polarity domains: a known property (Mori et al. 2008), with the reshaping done by curvature flow plus protrusion. The cut cell never regains its lost area or protein (66% of the twin's area at t=18), because protein is conserved and erased protein leaves the cell, so this repairs organization, not size. I did not run the polarity-erase arm, the rho*=0.4 contrast or a grid change.
